audit_criteria.remove_issue_test: Strip the social-issue label (eldercare/divorce/custody/inheritance/business succession). The specific people and relationship history must still create reader pull.
audit_criteria.scene_engine: There must be a concrete choice that must be made now and whose execution changes the relationship irreversibly; not merely a position debate.
audit_criteria.reader_drive: The next-page question must be what these specific people will do, not which side is morally correct.
audit_criteria.character_specificity: Replacing the family/couple with generic equivalents must materially damage the premise; otherwise the characters are templates.
audit_criteria.plausibility_simple_action: Normal communication, law, finance, mediation or operational fixes may change tactics but cannot dissolve the core conflict.

results.remove_issue_test: FAIL. Remove eldercare/house-sale framing and the premise has almost no individualized sibling history beyond one sacrifices time and one contributes money.
results.scene_engine: PARTIAL. 'Sell the house or take over care next month' is concrete, but it functions primarily as a policy/household allocation decision rather than a character-specific irreversible relational act.
results.reader_drive: FAIL_RISK. The natural reading question is largely who is fairer/right about care, money and the mother's home.
results.character_specificity: FAIL. It can be transplanted with minimal loss to thousands of sibling-caregiving families.
results.plausibility_simple_action: FAIL/PARTIAL. Nursing-home tiers, hiring care, renting/mortgaging the house, public benefits, rotating care, and revised cost-sharing can materially reshape the conflict; the premise does not yet show why those ordinary options have already failed.
results.user_fit: FAIL. Realistic, but likely to feel like a social-issue case discussion rather than immersive fiction.

results.remove_issue_test: PARTIAL. Marriage exhaustion survives the restaurant label, but the current premise gives little unique relational history beyond work consumed the marriage.
results.scene_engine: PARTIAL. Taking compensation to close versus reopen is concrete, but the wife has already stated she will not continue; that makes a clean separation of business/life a plausible endpoint rather than forcing an emotionally irreducible choice.
results.reader_drive: FAIL_RISK. The reader may mostly evaluate whether the husband should save the shop/employees or choose the marriage.
results.character_specificity: FAIL. Replace restaurant with a studio/shop/family business and the structure remains nearly identical.
results.plausibility_simple_action: FAIL/PARTIAL. Divide compensation, restructure ownership, hire management, husband reopen independently, negotiate debt allocation; these normal actions can reduce the conflict substantially.
results.user_fit: FAIL. More human than the twist batch, but still reads as a relationship/business dilemma template.

results.remove_issue_test: PARTIAL/PASS. Parent-child attachment and unequal care labor are human, but the current characterization is still almost entirely the custody/career issue.
results.scene_engine: PASS/PARTIAL. The father can accept the move or actually become primary caregiver; either changes family life materially.
results.reader_drive: PARTIAL. There is some interest in whether the father will accept the full burden, but the premise strongly invites a judgment about whether he only wants the easy parts of parenting.
results.character_specificity: FAIL. No unique history, habit, failure, promise, or child-specific bond makes these exact three people non-interchangeable.
results.plausibility_simple_action: PARTIAL. Mediation, adjusted schedules, remote work, relocation negotiation or shared-care changes cannot erase all cost, but they can turn the story into custody logistics unless more specific relational facts exist.
results.user_fit: FAIL_CURRENT_FORM. Emotion is possible, but it currently reads more like a family-court thought experiment than a novel engine.

results.remove_issue_test: PARTIAL. Recognition versus family loyalty survives the gender-inheritance label, but current people are archetypal: capable daughter, traditional father, absent son.
results.scene_engine: PASS/PARTIAL. Daughter resigning is a real act, yet the premise is built around a negotiation position rather than a specific relational wound/event.
results.reader_drive: FAIL_RISK. The reader is strongly prompted to decide whether the father is sexist/unfair rather than become curious about unpredictable behavior from specific people.
results.character_specificity: FAIL. The roles are highly replaceable and map directly onto a common social trope.
results.plausibility_simple_action: FAIL/PARTIAL. Management control, minority equity, vesting, buyout, customer-transition contracts or staged succession are ordinary options; if the father rejects all, the story risks making him a device to preserve the issue.
results.user_fit: FAIL_CURRENT_FORM. Clear anger potential, but too easy to become a thesis about gender/family-business succession.
